language.title: Choose your language
language.subtitle: Deepsand detected your system language. Choose the language you want to use; you can change it later in Settings.
language.sectionHint: The language Deepsand's interface is shown in.
language.nativeHint: Languages are listed in their own writing system.
network.noneDescription: Nothing is reachable except the model API itself. Package installs, git clones and web requests will all fail, as will anything the enabled tools would otherwise reach — the sandbox has no way out other than the address its model is served from.
network.internetDescription: Public internet is reachable. The host machine, your local network, link-local addresses and cloud metadata endpoints are blocked by the container's own kernel rules.
network.allowlistedDescription: Only what you list is reachable. A hostname you list goes through Deepsand's proxy; an address you list is reached directly, so a database or any non-HTTP client works. An entry with no port covers every port, and a port you list is also published on this machine's loopback so you can reach a server the sandbox runs there. A hostname that resolves into local or private address space is still refused — list the address itself to reach it on purpose.
network.fullDescription: No egress restriction at all, including this machine's own network services. Filesystem isolation is unaffected, but prefer a narrower mode.
network.label: Network access
docker.restartTitle: Restart Docker's engine — including the WSL process it runs in — and wait until a container can start again.
docker.restartCompact: Ends every container on this machine, then restarts Docker Desktop and its WSL process.
docker.restartDetail: This ends every container on this machine, including other projects' sandboxes. It restarts Docker Desktop and the WSL process its engine runs in, where Docker uses one.
docker.detailNotRunning: Docker Desktop is not running. Start it and try again.
docker.detailNoAnswer: Docker Desktop is running, but its daemon is not answering. It can take a minute to come up after starting; if it stays like this, restart Docker Desktop.
docker.detailDesktopLimited: Docker Desktop detected: the daemon runs inside a VM, so limited hardening options are available.
app.title: Deepsand
app.devModeTitle: A local build, not a released one
app.tagline: DeepCode runs inside a container that can only see the project you choose.
app.noProjectsHint: Create one to get a sandbox.
app.noProjectSelectedDetail: Create a project, give it a working directory, and run DeepCode inside a container that can only see that directory.
app.diskTitle: Total size of this project's folder on disk, including build output such as target/ and node_modules/. A physical file with more than one hard link is counted once.
app.diskTitlePartial: Some files could not be read, so this is a lower bound on the project folder's size. Build output such as target/ and node_modules/ is included; a physical file with more than one hard link is counted once.
projectRename.title: Rename project
projectRename.subtitle: Change the name shown in the sidebar.
projectRename.name: Project name
projectRename.hint: This changes the sidebar label only. The sandbox's container, state volume and saved sessions keep their existing internal names.
projectRename.renamedBody: Its container, state volume and saved sessions were not touched.
app.sandboxRestartedBody: The session resumed where it left off.
toast.revealProjectFailed: Could not open the project folder
toast.sessionBusyBody: If it has been a while, it is most likely building the project image, which takes minutes the first time. That build writes into the terminal, and the sandbox starts on its own when it finishes.
toast.sessionHungBody: Starting or stopping it has taken fifteen minutes without an answer, so the button is available again. It may still be working: the Activity tab and the log have the details.
toast.cancelBuildBody: Its output so far is in the Activity tab.
toast.restartingDeepCodeBody: The sandboxed process exited with code {code}. Starting it again.
toast.deepcodeKeepsExitingBody: It exited unexpectedly several times in a row, so it has been left stopped. Start the project again once the cause is fixed.
toast.accessGrantedBody: The sandbox is restarting with the new permission.
toast.toolsOutOfDateTitle: Cached tools are out of date
toast.toolsOutOfDateBody: {note} The next build installs them again.
activity.whatRunsDetail: The sandbox is one docker run command. This is the whole of it — there is no second path that starts a container, and nothing in it depends on the sandbox's own good behaviour.
activity.runtimeImageDetail: The image contains the DeepCode CLI and the sandbox entrypoint. Building it is the only step that needs network access on the host.
activity.requestsDiscardedDetail: Requests that arrived on the spool but failed validation. A sandbox can ask for anything, so Deepsand checks the shape of what arrives before it reaches your screen.
activity.blockedDestinationsDetail: Only applies to allowlisted network mode. Nothing appears here in internet mode because the blocking happens inside the container's kernel, where Deepsand cannot see individual attempts. Allowing a host adds it to this project's allowlist, not the app-wide one.
activity.allowTitle: Add this host to the egress allowlist
activity.logDetail: Every error the window shows is written here as well, so it can be read and copied after the box is gone.
activity.logPathOnClipboard: The log's path is on the clipboard.
perm.offDetail: Nothing this project asks for will reach you, and the sandbox is told not to ask rather than being left waiting. Anything it needs beyond the workspace, the shared directories and the network allowlist will simply fail. Turn this back on to be asked again.
perm.onDetail: The sandbox can ask for a directory, a network destination or a tool that is not installed, and you decide each one. Each request is written by the sandbox and is not authenticated, so read what it asks for before granting it. Turn this off if the requests have become noise — the setting is per project, and the dialog for a request can also turn it off.
perm.resumeHint: Resumes this sandbox on launch if it was running when you last closed the app. Off by default: a sandbox that comes back on its own is something you ask for.
perm.notConsulted: This project is in {mode} mode, so the allowlist below is not consulted. Choose Allowlisted above for these entries to take effect.
perm.allowlistHint: One entry per line. host matches exactly, *.host its subdomains, host/path only paths under that prefix (HTTP only — a CONNECT tunnel hides the path), !host denies and always wins, re:^…$ is an anchored regular expression.
perm.notEnforced: Not enforced — these entries would do nothing:
perm.broadDetail: {entries}. These allow far more than the hosts they name; consider narrowing them.
perm.showAllEntries: Show all {total} entries in force (including {global} inherited from global settings)
perm.globalHint: The global list is edited in the app-wide Settings dialog. Deny entries from either list beat allow entries from the other, so a global !host cannot be undone here.
perm.directoryGone: This directory is no longer on disk
perm.allowWriteTitle: Allow DeepCode to modify this directory
perm.noExtraDirectories: No extra directories are shared. The sandbox can only see /workspace.
perm.changesNextStart: Changes take effect when the sandbox next starts.
perm.shareDetail: Only the directories you list here become visible. Deepsand refuses system directories, your home folder, credential stores, anything overlapping its own state, and any path that would nest inside another share.
perm.readOnlyDetail: DeepCode can read files but cannot change or delete anything. Prefer this.
perm.readWriteDetail: DeepCode can create, modify and delete files in this directory.
perm.decisionLogDetail: Every grant, revoke and refusal for this project, newest last.
perm.couldNotReadAllowlist: Could not read this project's allowlist
perm.entryInForce: {count} entry in force for this project.
perm.entriesInForce: {count} entries in force for this project.
perm.restartForNetwork: Restart the sandbox for it to take effect.
perm.couldNotChangeNetwork: Could not change the network mode
perm.pathAllowedMount: Allowed. It would appear as a mount inside the sandbox.
perm.restartToAttach: Restart the sandbox to attach it.
perm.restartToDetach: Restart the sandbox to detach it.
perm.requestsOnBody: Requests from this project will reach you as they come in.
perm.requestsOffBody: Anything already waiting was refused, and the sandbox has been told not to ask.
perm.browseTitle: Choose a directory to share with this sandbox
secrets.couldNotRead: Could not read this project's secrets
secrets.title: Secrets for this project
secrets.detail: Stored encrypted, keyed from your operating system's keystore — not in the project directory, not in the repository, and never in the audit log. They are handed to the container as environment variables, so anything running inside the sandbox can read them, which is what makes them useful and also what makes a broad network allowlist a way for one to leave.
secrets.restartNeeded: A sandbox is running. Changes here are stored straight away but reach the container on its next start, so restart the sandbox after editing.
secrets.none: No secrets yet. Anything this project needs — an API key, a database URL — can go here rather than in a file in the repository.
secrets.name: Name
secrets.copyLabel: Copy the value to your clipboard
secrets.disableLabel: Disable: keep it stored, but stop handing it to the sandbox
secrets.enableLabel: Enable: hand it to the sandbox again
secrets.addHint: The name becomes an environment variable name, so it has to be one. Values are typed one way: once saved they are never shown again, only replaced.
secrets.nameLetters: Use letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter or underscore.
secrets.nameReservedPrefix: Names starting with DEEPSAND_ are reserved.
secrets.nameReserved: {name} is reserved, because the sandbox itself uses it.
secrets.savedRestart: Encrypted and stored. Restart the sandbox so it reaches the container.
secrets.savedNextStart: Encrypted and stored. It will be in the environment next time this project runs.
secrets.replacedBody: The old value is gone; it was overwritten, not kept.
secrets.copiedBody: The value is on your clipboard. It was never shown here.
secrets.disabledBody: Still stored and still replaceable, just not handed to the sandbox.
secrets.enabledBody: It will be in the environment next time this project starts.
secrets.renamedBody: The value and its on/off state came with it.
secrets.removedBody: Removed from the store and from the sandbox environment.
tools.modelAppliedLive: Written into the running sandbox's settings.
tools.modelSaved: Saved. It applies when this project next runs.
tools.customModelSubtitle: Used exactly as written: nothing checks it against the API's list.
tools.customModelDetail: Goes into the sandbox's MODEL setting as typed. Leave the dropdown on Defer to Config to go back to the configured model.
tools.modelTitleDefer: The model this project runs. Defer to Config follows the configured model.
tools.modelTitleConfigured: The model this project runs. Defer to Config follows the configured model ({model}).
tools.savedNextRun: Saved. It applies when this project next runs.

tools.defaultTitle: On for a new project unless switched off
tools.reachesHosts: Reaches {hosts} while switched on, and stops the moment it is switched off.
tools.couldNotRead: Could not read this project's tools
tools.rebuildToInstall: Rebuild the image to install them.
tools.rebuildToRemove: Rebuild the image to remove them.

tools.everyToolOffDetail: {network}The next build produces a bare image, with no git, jq or ripgrep.
tools.toolOnHosts: Also allowed: {hosts}. Rebuild the image to install it.
tools.rebuildToInstallOne: Rebuild the image to install it.
tools.rebuildToApply: Rebuild the image so it takes effect.

tools.imageTagTitle: The image tag this selection builds to
tools.detail: Tools are built into this project's container image, so a change here needs the image rebuilt before it takes effect. A tool that needs the network also opens the hosts it uses while it is switched on, and closes them again when switched off.
tools.openNow: Open for this project right now: {hosts}
tools.unavailableOne: 1 tool is greyed out and cannot be switched on, because the sandbox image is not the one it needs.
tools.unavailableMany: {count} tools are greyed out and cannot be switched on, because the sandbox image is not the one they need.
tools.enableAllTitle: Switch on every tool this image can hold, including package managers
tools.disableAllTitle: Switch everything off, including git, jq and ripgrep

terminal.runsInside: DeepCode will run inside a container whose only view of this machine is {rootDir}{extra}.
terminal.installingTools: Installing the tools this project asked for. The install is running above, in this terminal, and the project starts by itself as soon as it finishes.

terminal.couldNotReadClipboardBody: Use right-click then Paste in the terminal instead.
terminal.attachTooLarge: {name} is {size} MB; the limit is {limit} MB.
terminal.installingInBackground: Installing the tools in the background.

request.title.secretUnnamed: DeepCode is asking for a secret to be added to this project
request.stopAskingTitle: Stop {name} from asking for permissions at all. Anything already waiting is refused, and this request is refused too.
request.frozen: Nothing is running in the sandbox while this is open, so the agent cannot work ahead of your decision. If you take more than a minute, the call it was waiting on ends in a timeout — it collects your decision afterwards rather than guessing.
request.purpose: What it says it needs it for:
request.pathRecheck: Deepsand re-checks this path itself. A path it refuses cannot be granted even if you allow it.
request.networkHint: Allowing adds these to this project's allowlist only. A DENY entry in the global list still wins, so a host banned app-wide cannot be opened here.
request.toolHint: A tool is baked into the project's image, so it is not usable until the image is rebuilt and the sandbox restarted. DeepCode is told this, so it will not try to install it itself.
request.readOnlyDetail: It can read the files but cannot change or delete anything.
request.readWriteDetail: It can create, modify and delete files in this directory.
request.judgment: Deepsand cannot verify the agent is being honest, please use your best judgment.
request.pathAllowed: Allowed. It will appear inside the sandbox as /grants/<name>.
request.sharedTitle: Shared, and the sandbox is restarting
request.deniedBody: DeepCode was told the decision is final.
request.requestsOffBody: {name} cannot request permissions until you turn it back on, in Permissions.
newProject.subtitle: A project is a working directory plus the permissions DeepCode has inside it.
newProject.cloneHint: Clone a repository and use the clone as the project.
newProject.name: Name
newProject.pathUsable: Usable. It becomes /workspace inside the sandbox.
newProject.sandboxSees: The sandbox sees this directory at /workspace. It sees nothing else until you share something — not your home folder, not your other projects, and never a container-runtime socket.
newProject.createdBody: Run it when you are ready.
newProject.browseCloneTitle: Choose the directory to clone into
newProject.cloneHintLong: The repository is cloned into a new folder inside this directory. That cloned folder — not the directory you choose — becomes the project's working directory.
newProject.namePlaceholder: defaults to the repository's folder name
newProject.credentialsTried: The credentials already on this machine were tried first — git's stored credentials and its SSH keys — and the repository refused them.
newProject.enterCredentials: Enter a username and a personal access token for this host. They are used for this one clone and are not saved.
newProject.importedBody: The cloned folder is the project's working directory.
projectSettings.title: {name} settings
projectSettings.deepcodePrompts: DeepCode's own permission prompts inside the sandbox
projectSettings.modeHint: The container is the real boundary. Strict mode additionally makes DeepCode prompt for network, MCP and out-of-workspace access, with the prompts appearing in the terminal.
projectSettings.customTitle: This project's own prompt, typed below.
projectSettings.offTitle: Send no standing instructions in this project.
projectSettings.noGlobal: No app-wide prompt is set, so nothing is sent. Write one in Settings and it applies here and in every other project that is on Global.
projectSettings.customPlaceholder: For example: this repository is TypeScript only, and nothing is finished until npm test passes.
projectSettings.promptHint: The model is given this before anybody types anything, in every session of this project. It cannot widen what the sandbox reaches — an instruction that assumes more access is a reason to ask for it, not a permission — and it arrives whether or not your project has an AGENTS.md of its own.
projectSettings.inheritHint: Reads {path} at every start. Model: {model}, key {key}.
projectSettings.apiKeyPlaceholder: API key (leave blank to keep the current one)
projectSettings.wipeTitle: This permanently deletes this project's DeepCode conversation history and session data.
projectSettings.wipeDetail: DeepCode sessions, conversation history, attachments and skills stored in the sandbox will be removed. The sandbox is stopped first. The project folder {path} is not touched; the next start recreates DeepCode's settings and credentials from this machine.
projectSettings.wipeHint: Deletes the sandbox's conversation history, sessions, attachments and skills. Your project folder on disk is not touched. The sandbox is stopped first; DeepCode's settings and credentials are reinstalled on the next start.
projectSettings.savedBody: They apply the next time the sandbox starts.
projectSettings.wipedBody: The sandbox was stopped and its conversation history was removed. {path} was not touched.
projectSettings.couldNotWipe: Could not wipe the DeepCode data
settings.title: Settings
settings.userPromptPlaceholder: For example: explain the reasoning before the change, and never commit anything without asking.
settings.userPromptHint: Standing instructions the model is given before anybody types anything, in every project that has not set its own. Each project chooses between this, its own prompt, and none, in its settings. Saved as you type; a sandbox that is already running keeps the prompt it started with.
settings.networkHint: The mode every project you create from now on starts in. Allowlisted is the default and means default-deny: the model endpoint, the package registries in the global list, and whatever a project's tools need. Existing projects keep the mode they already have.
settings.fullWarning: Full egress removes the local-network block as well as the allowlist. Only choose this if the sandbox genuinely needs to reach machines on your own network.
settings.defaultCredentialsHint: Used when the host configuration and the project both say nothing. The API key below is kept in your operating system's keystore, not in Deepsand's state file.
settings.apiKeyHint: Kept in your operating system's keystore, never in Deepsand's state file. The window only ever shows the last four characters. Takes effect the next time a sandbox starts.
settings.apiKeyNone: No app-wide key is stored here.
settings.apiKeySaved: The key is now in your operating system's keystore.
settings.apiKeyRemoved: Deepsand will use the host configuration or a project override again.
settings.apiKeyCouldNotRead: Could not read the API key
settings.apiKeyCouldNotSave: Could not save the API key
settings.apiKeyCouldNotRemove: Could not remove the API key
settings.egressHint: Only used by the allowlisted network mode. A blanket * is ignored: use *.example.com to include subdomains. Ports 80 and 443 only.
settings.autoRestart: Restart the sandbox automatically when a permission is granted
settings.noNewPrivileges: Block privilege escalation inside the container
settings.netfilterRequired: Refuse to start if the network policy cannot be enforced
settings.hardeningHint: Docker Desktop runs the daemon inside a VM, so the hardened profile and AppArmor cannot be applied there. Deepsand says so in the plan preview rather than pretending otherwise.
settings.closeToTray: The close button hides Deepsand in the tray instead of stopping it
settings.closeHint: Off, closing does what it has always done: the sandboxes stop and Deepsand quits. On, the window disappears and everything keeps running — the tray icon opens it again, and its Quit stops the sandboxes.
settings.checkToolUpdates: Check the cached tools for newer versions at startup, and every six hours
settings.installWarning: Installing restarts Deepsand, which stops {target}. Anything the agent has not written to disk is lost, and the session has to be started again.
settings.toolCheckHint: The tool check asks npm and crates.io what they offer for the versions your cache holds, and empties that cache when something has moved, so the next build installs it again. It never builds anything by itself, and turning it off leaves the "Check now" button working. Updates are signed, and the signature is what Deepsand checks before installing — not the download. A release that is not signed with this project's key will be refused.
settings.couldNotChangeClosing: Could not change the closing behaviour
settings.couldNotCheckTools: Could not check the cached tools
settings.nothingNewer: Nothing in the cache has a newer version published.
settings.watchActivity: Watch progress in the Activity tab.
settings.startAtSignIn: Start Deepsand when I sign in.
settings.startupBackgroundHint: In the background it starts with no window at all — the tray icon opens it, and it is running so your sandboxes can be.
settings.startupUnreadable: The startup state could not be read on this system, so it cannot be changed from here.
settings.startupHint: Sandboxes still only start when you run them; a project set to run on its own is not affected by this.
settings.remoteAccessHint: Serve this GUI over HTTP so another device can reach it. Off by default, and the settings below only appear when it is on.
settings.remotePersistHint: Left off, the port closes when Deepsand exits. That is the safer default: a window opened for one afternoon should not still be open next month.
settings.lockoutHint: A locked-out address gets a "try again shortly" for five minutes; a correct token clears the count. Zero disables the limit, which is reasonable on a loopback-only server where the token is a formality.
settings.plainHttpWarning: Plain HTTP, so the access token crosses the network in clear text. Bind to 127.0.0.1 and put a reverse proxy in front for TLS and real authentication; that is also why every server defaults to loopback.
settings.copyManually: Select the token and copy it manually.
settings.capControl: Run and stop sandboxes, type into the terminal
settings.capGrant: Grant permissions: answer requests, mount directories, edit allowlists
settings.capHint: Granting permissions is what widens the sandbox boundary, so it is separate from simply driving an existing one.
settings.regenerateTitle: Issues a new token. Anything using the old one is cut off.
settings.tokenHint: Changing or regenerating a token takes effect when you apply, and cuts off anything still using the old one.
settings.uiMissing: The built frontend was not found, so the servers will answer the API but have no UI to serve. Run npm run build and rebuild the app.
tools.tool.jq.label: jq
tools.tool.jq.description: Command-line JSON processor, for reading and reshaping API responses.
tools.tool.ripgrep.label: ripgrep
tools.tool.ripgrep.description: Very fast recursive search. What the agent reaches for instead of grep -r.
tools.tool.curl.label: curl
tools.tool.curl.description: HTTP client, for fetching a URL the agent has been allowed to reach.
tools.tool.zip.label: zip / unzip
tools.tool.htmlq.label: htmlq
tools.tool.htmlq.description: CSS-selector queries over HTML, like jq for markup. Useful for scraping.
tools.tool.git.label: Git
tools.tool.git.description: Version control. On by default because a development sandbox without git is hard to use, but it is a tool like any other: switch it off and neither the binary nor the git config ships.
tools.tool.rea.label: REA (reverse engineering)
tools.tool.rea.description: Reverse-engineering analysis for shipped applications and binaries: Electron and JavaScript bundles, .NET assemblies, Go and Rust binaries, archives and PE resources. All analysis runs inside this sandbox.
tools.tool.rea.cost: Adds about 330 MB and a minute to the next build. Native decompilation needs Ghidra, Hopper or IDA, which this image does not carry.
tools.tool.dejared.label: Dejared (Java decompiler)
tools.tool.dejared.description: Explore and decompile Java .jar archives: list packages and resources, search classes and strings, read class metadata, and decompile to Java with CFR, Vineflower or Procyon. Runs inside this sandbox with its own Java 17 runtime. A Spring Boot fat-jar, WAR, EAR or AAR stores classes under a nested prefix and should be unpacked first.
tools.tool.dejared.cost: Adds a Java 17 runtime and about 25 MB of decompiler JAR, and a minute to the next build.
tools.tool.ffdec.label: FFDec (Flash decompiler)
tools.tool.ffdec.description: Analyze, decompile and patch Shockwave Flash (SWF) files: tags, classes, symbols, ActionScript, bytecode, constants and traits, then save the modified SWF. The JPEXS FFDec CLI is included for exports the MCP surface does not cover.
tools.tool.ffdec.cost: Adds a Java 25 runtime, the FFDec MCP server and the JPEXS FFDec CLI: about 230 MB and a minute to the next build.
tools.tool.web-search.label: Web search
tools.tool.web-search.description: DeepCode's own web search. Needs the vendor's API, so it also opens that API in the network filter while it is on.
tools.tool.node.label: Node.js
tools.tool.node.description: JavaScript runtime. Already in the base image; enabling asserts the newest line.
tools.tool.npm.label: npm
tools.tool.npm.description: JavaScript package manager, updated to the newest release.
tools.tool.xvfb.label: Virtual display (Xvfb)
tools.tool.xvfb.description: A screen that exists only inside this container, for programs that want one. Nothing appears on the operator's screen, and screenshots are taken of the display itself.
tools.tool.puppeteer.label: Puppeteer
tools.tool.puppeteer.description: A browser controlled from Node, with its own copy of Chromium. Renders into the virtual display when one is enabled, so pages behave as they do for a person.
tools.tool.puppeteer.cost: Adds about 850 MB to this project's image, and a couple of minutes to the next build: a browser, unpacked, plus the libraries it links against.
tools.tool.wrangler.label: Wrangler
tools.tool.wrangler.description: Cloudflare's CLI for Workers, Pages and their KV, R2 and D1 stores.
tools.tool.python.label: Python 3
tools.tool.python.description: Python runtime with pip and a virtualenv module.
tools.tool.cargo.label: Rust / cargo
tools.tool.cargo.description: Rust toolchain via rustup, in the sandbox user's home.
tools.tool.cargo.cost: Minutes of compiling the first time this image is built, plus the Rust toolchain.
tools.tool.go.label: Go
tools.tool.go.description: Go toolchain, installed from the official tarball.
tools.tool.apt.label: apt
tools.tool.apt.description: Let the agent install Debian packages itself. This is the base image's own package manager, and it can install almost anything, so treat it as the widest of these.
tools.tool.apk.label: apk
tools.tool.brew.label: Homebrew
tools.tool.brew.description: Homebrew on Linux. Self-contained under the sandbox user's home.
tools.tool.nix.label: Nix
tools.tool.nix.description: Nix with flakes. Gives reproducible per-project toolchains, at the cost of a large image and a slower first build.
